item.title: Science and research
item.description: Words for describing experiments, findings and how research is done.

children.definition: an idea that is suggested as an explanation and can then be tested
children.example: Their hypothesis was that students who sleep more remember more vocabulary.

children.definition: a small group chosen from a larger population to be studied
children.example: With a sample of only twenty people, the results are hard to generalise.

children.definition: a factor in an experiment that can change or be changed
children.example: Temperature was the only variable they changed during the test.

children.definition: the people in a study who do not receive the treatment, used for comparison
children.example: The control group took a pill with no active ingredient.

children.definition: the checking of a study by other experts before it is published
children.example: The paper is still going through peer review.

children.definition: to repeat a study to see if you get the same results
children.example: Other labs failed to replicate the original findings.

children.definition: the information that a study discovers
children.example: The findings suggest that short daily practice works better than long sessions.

children.definition: an important discovery that suddenly makes progress possible
children.example: The new battery design could be a breakthrough for electric cars.

children.definition: a connection between two things that change together, which may not mean one causes the other
children.example: There is a correlation between ice cream sales and sunburn, but ice cream doesn't cause sunburn.

children.definition: money given by an organisation for a particular project
children.example: The team applied for funding to study water quality in the Fergana Valley.

children.definition: a tendency that makes results unfair or not accurate
children.example: Asking only your friends to fill in the survey introduces bias.

children.definition: proving something so that there is no more doubt
children.example: So far there is no conclusive evidence that the supplement works.
